patients.summary: Retired textile worker treated for right breast IDC in 2018 who joined the practice in 2021, had a bone-metastatic recurrence in 2022, then severe vitamin D deficiency with osteomalacia, cachexia and progressive disease, and moved to home hospice after a 2026 family meeting.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Daughter phoned on behalf of her mother, Mei Zhang, 64. Mother has had no regular doctor for several years, only her cancer doctors. Explained membership, fees and that insurance still covers labs and specialists. Daughter will help with paperwork. New patient slot given for 9/8 at 9:30, 60 min. Asked them to bring all pill bottles and any cancer treatment paperwork they have at home.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT
64F here with her daughter to set up primary care. Says she has not had a family doctor in several years; her care since 2018 has all been at the cancer center.

ONCOLOGIC HX: Invasive ductal carcinoma, right breast, diagnosed 2018. Right modified radical mastectomy with axillary node dissection 2018. Adjuvant chemo through a right subclavian port, then radiation to the right chest wall. Port still in. Finished treatment, now seen in surveillance by her oncologist. She does not know her stage or tumor markers; daughter thinks the paperwork is at the cancer center. Will request a summary.

PMH: as above, otherwise nothing she knows of.
PSH: R MRM with ALND; port placement.
MEDS: none.
ALLERGIES: sulfa (hives), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).
FHx: mother had breast cancer after menopause, found at 55, has since died. Maternal aunt with ovarian cancer. Father with high blood pressure.
SOCIAL: Retired, worked many years in a textile mill. Married, lives with husband in Easthampton. Daughter close by and helps with appointments. Never smoked. No alcohol.

ROS: no weight change she has noticed, no bone pain, no cough, appetite ok.

EXAM: small, thin woman, pleasant, English fluent. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Right chest: healed mastectomy scar, no nodularity along the scar or chest wall, port site clean. Left breast without mass, no axillary or supraclavicular adenopathy. Abdomen soft, no liver edge. Spine nontender. No edema.

A/P
1. Hx R breast cancer, treated 2018, in surveillance. Request oncology summary. Oncology owns surveillance imaging.
2. Family hx breast/ovarian cancer. Asked whether genetics was ever done; she is not sure. Will look in the oncology records.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c today. Hep C and HIV screen once, ok with her. FIT kit given. Flu shot when the vaccine arrives, nurse visit. Medicare starts next spring, will do the welcome visit then.
RTC spring, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hello Mrs. Zhang, your blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol all came back normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Nothing to change. Please drop off the stool kit when you can. Best, your primary care physician

documents.title: Oncology treatment summary (outside oncology group)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
TREATMENT SUMMARY - MEDICAL ONCOLOGY
Patient: Mei Zhang  DOB 03/29/1957
Prepared at request of primary care.

Diagnosis: invasive ductal carcinoma, right breast, 2018.
Surgery: right modified radical mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection, 2018.
Vascular access: right subclavian implanted port, placed 2018, maintained with periodic flushes.
Systemic therapy: adjuvant chemotherapy, completed 2018.
Radiation: adjuvant radiation to the right chest wall, completed 2018.
Current status: no evidence of disease at last surveillance visit. Surveillance visits every 6 months with yearly imaging of the left breast.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (urticaria), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis) - avoid IV contrast or premedicate per radiology.
Medications: none.

Please contact our office with questions.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed oncology summary. No stage, receptor or genetics information included. Fine for now; she is followed there.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Screening questions negative. Influenza vaccine IM left deltoid (no injections or BP on the right arm per mastectomy). Tolerated, observed 15 min. She states COVID primary series done at a pharmacy this spring; card not with her, will bring next time.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat in a year. Letter to pt.

reports.text: LEFT MAMMOGRAM, SURVEILLANCE. History: right mastectomy 2018 for invasive ductal carcinoma. Technique: standard CC and MLO views of the left breast. Comparison: prior study from last year. Breast composition: scattered areas of fibroglandular density. There is no suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcification. Skin and nipple unremarkable. No axillary adenopathy in the imaged field.
reports.conclusion: No mammographic evidence of malignancy, left breast. BI-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual surveillance.

documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Report received by fax from the cancer center's breast imaging service. Study date 11/30/2021. Negative, BI-RADS 1. Reviewed by PCP.

procedures.procedure: Initial preventive physical examination (Welcome to Medicare)

documents.title: Welcome to Medicare Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
IPPE. Turned 65 last week, Medicare now primary with a supplement.
Feels well. Walks to the corner store, does her own cooking. Last oncology visit in winter was fine per pt.
Functional screen: independent in ADLs and IADLs, husband drives. No falls. Hearing and vision fine with readers. Home safe, one-floor living.
PHQ-2 0.
Meds: none. Allergies: sulfa, iodinated contrast.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear, heart regular. Chest wall unchanged, port site clean. No adenopathy. Spine and hips nontender. Gait steady.

Plan:
- PCV20 and first Shingrix today, left arm. Second Shingrix in 2-6 months.
- Colon: FIT negative 11/2021, repeat this fall.
- Breast: left side imaging per oncology, last one negative.
- Bone density: will raise with oncology whether they want a DXA.
- Advance directive: gave her the health care proxy form; she wants her daughter as proxy. Will bring it back.
Follow up 6 months.

documents.title: Office Visit - back and hip pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 3-4 weeks of aching between the shoulder blades and in the right hip. Worse at night, not better lying down. No fall or lifting injury. No leg weakness, numbness, bladder or bowel change. No fever.
PMH right breast IDC 2018, s/p MRM, chemo, chest wall radiation.

O: Vitals as charted. Tender to percussion over the mid thoracic spine. Right hip with discomfort at end range internal rotation, no deformity, bears weight. Strength 5/5 legs, reflexes symmetric, sensation intact. Gait normal.

A/P: New night-predominant thoracic spine and right hip pain in a breast cancer survivor. Recurrence in bone has to be excluded first. Neuro intact today.
- Called her oncologist's office while she was here; they will bring her in this week and arrange restaging imaging (they know about the contrast allergy).
- Return precautions reviewed with her and daughter: any leg weakness, numbness or trouble with urine or stool means the ED today.
- Will touch base after oncology sees her.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of breast
conditions.note: right breast invasive ductal carcinoma, metastatic recurrence, stage IV, widespread osseous metastases

documents.title: Results from cancer center
documents.author: patient
documents.body: (written by daughter) Hi doctor, wanted you to know the scans and the biopsy at the cancer center show the breast cancer came back and is in many of her bones, including her back and the right hip. They called it stage 4. She will start radiation to her back next week and then a new treatment. They gave her stronger pain pills. We are all pretty shaken. Thank you for calling them so fast.

documents.title: RE: Results from cancer center
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I am so sorry to hear this, and thank you for letting me know. I've updated her chart. Her oncology team will lead the cancer treatment; I'm here for everything else, including help with side effects, and for all of you. I'll call in a few weeks to see how radiation is going. Please send me the names and doses of the new pain medicines when you have them.

Take 1 tablet by mouth every 4 hours as needed for breakthrough pain
Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Check-in call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spoke with pt and daughter (speakerphone). Radiation to the thoracic spine finished last week, back pain noticeably better. Started a new IV treatment at the cancer center through her port. Hip still aches with walking.
Daughter read me the bottles, all from oncology: morphine ER 30 mg q12h, morphine IR 15 mg q4h prn (using 1-2 a day), senna 8.6 mg bid, docusate 100 mg bid, prochlorperazine 10 mg q6h prn nausea. Bowels were stuck the first week on morphine, better since the senna and docusate. Nausea mild, on treatment days.
No leg weakness or numbness. Eating less but ok.
Med list updated. Reminded her not to stop the bowel regimen while on morphine. Office visit in the fall, sooner if needed. Asked oncology to fax their notes.

documents.title: Medical oncology consultation letter, June 2022
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - OUTPATIENT NOTE
Date of service: 06/02/2022
Referring: primary care

Ms. Zhang is a 65-year-old woman with a history of right breast invasive ductal carcinoma treated in 2018 with mastectomy and axillary dissection, adjuvant chemotherapy and chest wall radiation, who was sent back to us by her primary care physician for new thoracic back and right hip pain.

Restaging imaging (done without iodinated contrast given her allergy) shows widespread osseous metastases, including the thoracic spine and the right hip. Bone biopsy confirms metastatic carcinoma consistent with her breast primary.

Impression: Stage IV invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast with widespread osseous metastases. No cord compression.

Plan:
- Palliative radiation to the thoracic spine, arranged with radiation oncology.
- Begin palliative systemic therapy here; regimen and schedule discussed with patient and daughter.
- Pain: morphine sulfate ER 30 mg every 12 hours; morphine sulfate IR 15 mg every 4 hours as needed for breakthrough pain.
- Bowel regimen: senna 8.6 mg twice daily, docusate 100 mg twice daily.
- Prochlorperazine 10 mg every 6 hours as needed for nausea.
- Follow-up in clinic with labs before each cycle.

Allergies: sulfa drugs (urticaria), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).

cc: primary care physician

documents.title: Letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: June oncology letter finally arrived. Matches what the family told me in June and July. Problem and med lists already reflect it. Filed.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Timed between treatment cycles; oncology ok'd. High-dose flu, Shingrix #2 and bivalent COVID booster, all left arm. No reactions during observation. Shingrix series now complete.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with daughter. Four months into treatment for the bone recurrence. Back pain much better since radiation; right hip still sore with walking, uses a cane outside now. Takes the ER morphine twice a day and 1 IR most days. Bowels every 1-2 days on senna/docusate. Some nausea the day after treatment, prochlorperazine helps. Appetite down, has lost about 3 kg since spring.

Exam: thin, tired-appearing. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Port site clean. Mild tenderness over the right hip. No spinal tenderness today. Neuro grossly intact. No edema.

A/P
1. Stage IV R breast IDC with bone mets - per oncology, on palliative systemic therapy.
2. Cancer pain - controlled on oncology's morphine regimen. Oncology prescribes; we won't co-prescribe.
3. Opioid-induced constipation - controlled.
4. Weight loss - on treatment; encouraged small frequent meals, protein with each meal. Recheck weight next visit.
CBC/CMP today since she's here (oncology draws too). Flu, COVID and Shingrix done last month. FIT not repeated given active metastatic disease. RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mrs. Zhang, your blood count is a little low, which is common during treatment. Kidney function is normal. The alkaline phosphatase, a bone enzyme, is up a bit, which goes with the bone involvement your oncologist is treating. I've forwarded the results to them. Nothing new for you to do.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Interval: continues treatment at the cancer center every few weeks. Daughter drives. Pain mostly in the right hip now, worse late in the day. Uses IR morphine once or twice daily on top of the ER. Bowels ok. Tired on treatment weeks. Eating maybe half of what she used to, mostly rice and soup.
No falls. No new back pain, no leg weakness.

Exam: thin, NAD. Lungs clear, heart regular. Port site clean. Right hip tender laterally, ROM limited by pain. Walks with cane.

A/P
- Metastatic breast cancer, bone - on oncology's regimen.
- Cancer pain - acceptable per her; plan and refills with oncology.
- Poor intake, weight drifting down - asked her to mention it to oncology; they may want to add something for appetite. Daughter will bring a 3-day food log next time.
RTC 3 months, annual wellness visit.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Fill history update
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fill report shows new Rx: mirtazapine 15 mg, 1 tab at bedtime, #30, filled 3/9, prescriber oncology. No letter from oncology. Called daughter: yes, oncologist started it for appetite and sleep. Added to med list as outside med. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Seen. Reasonable choice. No interacting meds on our list. Will review at April visit.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, with daughter.
Weight continues down, 4 kg since October. Oncology started mirtazapine 15 mg at night in March for appetite; she thinks she sleeps better, appetite a little better, not much. Food log: rice, instant noodles, tea, some fruit. Little protein. Rarely outside now beyond appointments.
Function: needs help with shopping and cleaning now, still bathes and dresses herself. No falls. Husband home with her.
PHQ-2 1. Says she is sad sometimes about the cancer but not depressed.
Cognition: clock and recall normal.
Health care proxy: daughter, form on file.

Exam: cachectic, temporal wasting. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft. Right hip tender. Uses cane.

A/P
1. Cancer anorexia-cachexia - added to problem list. On mirtazapine per oncology. Protein with every meal, oral supplement drinks between meals; daughter to stock them.
2. Metastatic breast ca to bone, cancer pain, opioid constipation - unchanged, oncology managing.
3. Labs today.
Vaccines current. Screening deferred given active metastatic disease. RTC 3 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: proximal weakness and diffuse bone pain, question of metabolic bone disease

documents.title: Office Visit - fatigue and weakness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, aching all over, can't get out of a chair.
S: Over 6-8 weeks, more fatigue and a deep ache in the shins and arms, different from her hip pain. Last few weeks needs to push off with both hands to stand from a chair and pull on the rail for stairs. No new focal back pain. Bowels ok. Oncology says her treatment is going about as expected.

O: Thin. Hip flexors and deltoids 4/5 bilaterally, distal strength normal. Rises from chair only with arms. Bones of the lower legs and forearms tender to pressure. Reflexes symmetric. Sensation intact.

A/P: Proximal weakness with diffuse bone tenderness away from her known metastatic sites. Could be disease, but the pattern and her diet and limited time outdoors make a metabolic bone problem worth looking for. Referral to endocrinology; asked them to see her soon. Let oncology know. Return sooner if new back pain, leg numbness or trouble with bladder/bowel.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times daily with meals

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/17/2023
Reason: fatigue, generalized bone discomfort, difficulty standing from seated. Referred by primary care.

HPI: 66-year-old woman with stage IV right breast IDC metastatic to bone, on palliative therapy with her oncologist, seen for fatigue, aching bones and new trouble getting up from a chair over the past two months. Her diet is mostly rice and instant noodles and she seldom gets outdoors.

Medications: morphine ER 30 mg q12h, morphine IR 15 mg q4h prn, senna 8.6 mg bid, docusate 100 mg bid, prochlorperazine 10 mg q6h prn, mirtazapine 15 mg qhs.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).
Family history: mother breast cancer at 55 (deceased); maternal aunt ovarian cancer; father hypertension.
Social: retired textile worker, never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: thin woman. Weakness of the proximal muscles in arms and legs. Both tibias and both forearms are tender when pressed. Gait is wide-based. Mild kyphosis.

Labs today: calcium 7.3 mg/dL, phosphate 1.9 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 230 U/L, 25-hydroxyvitamin D 6 ng/mL, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D undetectable.
DXA: bone mineral density decreased, pattern consistent with osteomalacia.

Impression:
1. Severe vitamin D deficiency with osteomalacia.
2. Hypocalcemia from the above; phosphate also low.
3. Sarcopenia, from her malignancy and vitamin D deficiency together.

Plan:
- Cholecalciferol 50,000 units by mouth once weekly.
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg by mouth three times daily with meals.
- Dietary counseling given: dairy or fortified soy, fish, eggs; daylight exposure as able.
- Recheck calcium, phosphorus and 25-hydroxyvitamin D in about 3 months; primary care may draw.
- Will copy oncology.

Thank you for this referral.

orders.reason: 3-month recheck on vitamin D and calcium
3-month recheck on vitamin D and calcium
3-month recheck on vitamin D and calcium

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after endo. Read their letter: vitamin D 6, calcium 7.3, phos 1.9, ALP 230, osteomalacia on DXA. Now on cholecalciferol 50,000 units weekly and calcium carbonate 600 mg with each meal. Taking both; daughter set up a pill box. The calcium tablets are large, she cuts them in half.
Says the shin aching is a little less already. Still pushes up from chairs.

Exam: vitals ok. Proximal weakness unchanged. No Chvostek. Lungs clear.

A/P
- Vitamin D deficiency with osteomalacia, hypocalcemia, sarcopenia: added to list, endo plan in place. Recheck Ca/phos/vit D late October, I'll draw here.
- Calcium is better tolerated split with meals; ok to keep cutting tablets.
- Flu/COVID in September.
RTC after the October labs.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose influenza and 2023-24 COVID vaccine, left deltoid, between treatment cycles. Pt in wheelchair from the car today for the long hallway, walks short distances with cane. No reactions.

documents.title: Lab draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Venipuncture left arm (no right arm draws). Tolerated.

documents.title: Vitamin D and calcium results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: vitamin D is up from 6 to 22, calcium from 7.3 to 8.7 and phosphorus from 1.9 to 2.9. Moving the right way. Keep taking the weekly vitamin D and the calcium with meals. I'm sending a copy to endocrinology.

documents.title: RE: Vitamin D and calcium results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: (daughter) Thank you! She says her legs ache less. Should she keep the same dose forever?

documents.title: RE: Vitamin D and calcium results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: For now yes, same doses. We'll recheck at her spring physical and go from there.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter check. Daughter here. Treatment continues at the cancer center; per pt oncologist pleased enough. Hip pain stable on the morphine. Bone aching in the legs much less since vitamin D. Still weak getting up but better than summer. Weight down another 2 kg. Eats more with the mirtazapine than before, still small portions.

Exam: cachectic. Lungs clear, heart regular. Proximal strength 4/5, rises with arm push. Right hip tender. Port ok.

A/P
1. Hypocalcemia - resolved on October labs; removing from list. Recheck CMP today.
2. Vitamin D deficiency/osteomalacia - continue current doses, vitamin D level at April AWV.
3. Cachexia/sarcopenia - continue supplements and mirtazapine. Offered home PT; prefers to wait.
4. Metastatic breast cancer - per oncology.
RTC April AWV.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.
Health risk review with pt and daughter. Needs help with shopping, cooking and cleaning; husband and daughter share these. Bathes with a shower chair. No falls since last year. Uses cane indoors, wheelchair for longer distances.
PHQ-2 1. Cognition intact on screen. Hearing/vision ok.
Advance care: proxy is daughter. Talked briefly about what matters most to her; she wants to be home and to see her family's events. Not ready yet for a full goals-of-care conversation, would like to come back to it.

Exam: cachectic, alert. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Right hip tender. Proximal weakness unchanged.

Plan:
- Vitamin D level today.
- Personalized plan given: protein intake, supplements, home exercise sheet for sit-to-stand.
- RSV vaccine in the fall with flu and COVID.
- Routine cancer screening not indicated given metastatic disease.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Vitamin D result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vitamin D is 31 now, in the normal range. Keep going as you are.

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Daughter called to cancel 6/11, mother has an infusion that day that was moved. Will call back to reschedule after her July oncology visit.

documents.title: Medical oncology follow-up, July 2024
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 07/29/2024

Interval history: Ms. Zhang, 67, with stage IV invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast metastatic to bone, continues palliative systemic therapy. Since her last visit she has more fatigue and is finding it harder to keep up with daily tasks. Her granddaughter graduates at an outdoor ceremony in about three months and she very much wants to be there; she worries she will not have the stamina. She feels well supported at home. Endocrinology saw her last summer for weakness and bone aches.

Medications: morphine sulfate ER 30 mg q12h; morphine sulfate IR 15 mg q4h prn breakthrough pain; cholecalciferol 50,000 units weekly; calcium carbonate 600 mg tid with meals; senna 8.6 mg bid; docusate 100 mg bid; prochlorperazine 10 mg q6h prn nausea; mirtazapine 15 mg qhs.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).

Vitals stable. Exam: cachectic. Diffuse tenderness over bone.

Labs: hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL, calcium 10.5 mg/dL, albumin 3.0 g/dL.

Assessment/Plan: Metastatic breast cancer to bone on palliative therapy, with fatigue and declining function. Continue current treatment. Discussed pacing and rest before the graduation; wheelchair for the event. No medication changes. Return in 6-8 weeks.

(Sent at the request of the primary care office.)

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from June. Saw oncology 7/29. Per pt and daughter: more tired, treatment continues, "blood a little low", no med changes. Her goal is her granddaughter's graduation this fall, outdoors; wants to be well enough to sit through it.
Tired most afternoons. Pain about the same. Eating small amounts. Bowels ok.

Exam: cachectic, in wheelchair today. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Diffuse bony tenderness, worst right hip.

A/P
- Metastatic breast ca/bone, fatigue - per oncology. We do not have the July note; front desk to request it.
- Graduation planning: pace the day, rest beforehand, IR morphine before leaving the house, wheelchair, shade and water. She liked that plan.
- Vit D/calcium - continue.
RTC after flu shots / early winter.

documents.body: Second request to the cancer center for the 7/29 oncology note (first request faxed 8/13). They have no record of the fax. Re-faxed with signed release. Was told 2-3 weeks.

documents.author: PCP

AWV. Pt with daughter; husband waited in the car.
Now needs help with bathing and dressing most days; husband helps mornings, daughter evenings and weekends and handles the pill box and all appointments. Wheelchair outside the house.

documents.title: Medical oncology visit, July 2025
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - CLINIC NOTE
Date of service: 07/21/2025

Ms. Zhang is a 68-year-old with stage IV invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast with osseous metastases, accompanied today by her daughter. She had periods of response early on, but the disease has now progressed. Over three years she has received several lines of chemotherapy and targeted therapy. She reports worsening fatigue and poor appetite, and her pain is not well controlled on her oral opioid regimen. She tells us she would like to put her quality of life first rather than continue with aggressive treatment.

Her daughter, who manages her medications and care, says she is overwhelmed by the amount she is handling.

Medications: morphine sulfate ER 30 mg q12h; morphine sulfate IR 15 mg q4h prn breakthrough pain; cholecalciferol 50,000 units weekly; calcium carbonate 600 mg tid with meals; senna 8.6 mg bid; docusate 100 mg bid; prochlorperazine 10 mg q6h prn nausea; mirtazapine 15 mg qhs.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).

Vitals stable. Exam: cachectic, seated in a wheelchair. Lungs clear.

Labs: hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, calcium 10.2 mg/dL, albumin 3.0 g/dL, creatinine 1.2 mg/dL.

Assessment/Plan: Progressive metastatic breast cancer. Treatment options and her priorities discussed at length; she will think about next steps with her family. Medications unchanged today. We encourage involving her primary care physician in planning for support at home.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Oncology note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Oncology note in. Progression, pt leaning toward quality-of-life focus, daughter overwhelmed. Asked front desk to get her in within 2 weeks with daughter and husband if possible.

Long visit, pt with daughter; husband joined by phone.
Oncology note 7/21 reviewed: disease progressing, Hgb 9.8, Ca 10.2, albumin 3.0, Cr 1.2. Pt reiterates she wants to focus on how she feels and is weighing whether to continue treatment.
Daughter: works part time, sets up all meds, drives to every appointment, up most nights checking on her mother. Says she is at the end of her rope. Husband does meals and daytime help but has trouble getting her on and off the toilet.
Pt: tired, wants to stay home. Pain worse some evenings despite IR doses; she will raise doses with oncology, who prescribe.

Exam: cachectic, in wheelchair. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Diffuse bony tenderness.

A/P
1. Caregiver strain / not enough support at home - home health referral for nursing (med management, pain review) and aide for bathing; she qualifies as homebound. Gave daughter caregiver support group info.
2. Progressive metastatic breast cancer - treatment decisions with oncology; offered a family meeting here whenever they are ready.
3. Pain - oncology to adjust; asked daughter to message them this week.
4. Creatinine 1.2, up from her usual - recheck with next labs.
RTC fall.

Video, pt in her bed at home, daughter holding the tablet.
Home health nurse weekly, aide helps with bathing; daughter says that has made a real difference. Pt still on treatment at the cancer center but tired for days after each one. Pain worse in the evenings. Appetite poor.
No new symptoms reported.
Observed: thin, speaking full sentences, comfortable at rest.

A/P: Progressive metastatic breast cancer with growing needs at home. She and family are talking about whether to stop treatment; oncology visit next month. Repeated offer of a family meeting here. Labs to be drawn before that meeting. Continue current meds per oncology.

documents.title: Family meeting
documents.author: patient
documents.body: (daughter) Hello doctor. Mom saw the cancer doctor last week. The new scans show the cancer has spread more and they said there is no treatment left that will help it. Mom says she is done with treatments anyway. She is more tired, sometimes short of breath, and the pain is harder to control. Can we have that family meeting with you? My father and I will both come. Thank you.

documents.title: RE: Family meeting
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, of course. Front desk will call to set an hour-long time next week. I'm ordering blood work for a couple of days before so we have current numbers. If her breathing gets worse before then, call us right away.

documents.body: Drawn in the car per family request, left arm. Tolerated.

documents.title: Family Meeting - Goals of Care
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
FAMILY MEETING. Present: patient, husband, daughter. 75 minutes, more than half on advance care planning.

Background: R breast IDC 2018, metastatic to bone since 2022, several lines of chemo and targeted therapy plus radiation. Per family, oncology's latest scans show widespread progression and her oncologist has told them nothing further is expected to control the cancer.

Her words: she is tired of treatments and wants the time she has left to be comfortable, at home, with family. She does not want to go back to the hospital unless it's the only way to keep her comfortable.
Symptoms: tired most of the day, short of breath now and then with exertion, pain harder to keep down even with extra IR doses.
Home: lives with husband, who does most of the day-to-day care and admits he can't keep up as her needs grow. Daughter handles meds and appointments. Home health aide 3x/week.

Labs 1/27: Hgb 9.2, Ca 11.4, alk phos 240, Cr 1.8.

Exam: pale, frail, in wheelchair. Breath sounds diminished at both bases. Heart regular. Spine and right hip tender to touch. Calm, engaged in the discussion.

A/P
1. Progressive stage IV breast cancer with bone metastases - patient chooses comfort-focused care. Hospice referral placed today, home hospice. Explained what hospice provides: nurse visits, aide, equipment, 24/7 phone line, medications for comfort.
2. Code status / MOLST - completed and signed with patient: DNR, DNI, comfort-focused treatment, no hospital transfer unless needed for comfort. Copy to family for the refrigerator, copy scanned.
3. Calcium 11.4 - stopping the calcium carbonate and the weekly vitamin D. Not chasing it further given her goals.
4. Pain and breathlessness - hospice team to take over adjusting the morphine; until admission continue current doses and use the IR as prescribed.
5. Caregiver strain - hospice aide hours and respite discussed.
I'll stay involved as her primary physician. Family has the office cell for anything before hospice starts.

documents.title: Hospice admission notice
documents.author: hospice
documents.body:
HOSPICE ADMISSION NOTIFICATION
Patient: Mei Zhang  DOB 03/29/1957
Admission date: 02/04/2026, routine home care.
Terminal diagnosis: malignant neoplasm of breast with secondary malignant neoplasm of bone.
Attending physician of record: primary care physician (as elected by patient).
Code status: DNR/DNI per MOLST dated 01/29/2026.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).
Medications on admission: morphine sulfate ER 30 mg q12h, morphine sulfate IR 15 mg q4h prn, senna 8.6 mg bid, docusate 100 mg bid, prochlorperazine 10 mg q6h prn, mirtazapine 15 mg qhs. Hospice team will adjust the comfort regimen as needed.
RN case manager visits twice weekly; aide visits; chaplain and social work offered and accepted.
Please sign and return the certification of terminal illness.

documents.title: Call with hospice RN
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hospice RN case manager called with an update. Pt settled, sleeping more, eating little. Pain better since the hospice team adjusted her regimen. Family coping better with the extra aide visits. Certification signed and returned last month. Plan a video visit with family in April.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - home hospice
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video with pt, husband and daughter at home. On home hospice since early February.
Pt in a hospital bed in the living room, by the window. Says she is comfortable most days. Sleeps much of the day, wakes for meals of congee and tea. Breathing ok at rest. Pain manageable, hospice adjusts her medicines. Bowels moving with help.
Family: tired but say hospice has lifted a lot off them; daughter sleeps through most nights now.
Observed: thin, alert, smiling, speaking in short sentences, no distress.

A/P: Metastatic breast cancer on home hospice, comfort goals being met. MOLST in the home. Hospice manages day-to-day medications; our list stays as of the January meeting. Family knows to call hospice first and can reach me anytime. No further visits scheduled; will check in through hospice.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: (daughter) Just a note to say Mom is peaceful. Her granddaughter visited this weekend and she was awake for most of it. Thank you for everything.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for writing. I'm glad she had that time with family. Thinking of all of you.

HOSPICE - BENEFIT PERIOD RECERTIFICATION
Patient: Mei Zhang

Comfort goals being met per patient and family. Symptom regimen managed by hospice team.
Please sign and return.
